mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a fall in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,400K signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 1400 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market slack, which reduces wage growth and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates weakening manufacturing activity and lower corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise of more than 0.5 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall of more than 2% in industrial production (INDPRO) within a single month signals a synchronized labor and supply shock, which increases recession risk and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous +0.5pp AND INDPRO < previous -2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 3% during a period of negative GDP growth (GDPC1) signals an emergency monetary easing, which boosts risk appetite and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3.0% AND GDPC1 YoY < 0% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase of more than 0.3 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for four consecutive months signals persistent labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.3pp for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% from the previous month, combined with a decline in personal consumption expenditures growth (implied from GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a consumer-driven recession and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > +5% AND GDPC1 monthly change < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.
